sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Single-Origin Green Arabica Coffee Bean Container Distribution

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition) with unitary national legislation influenced by French and Belgian company and commercial law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Avoidance Convention (1996, as amended by 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg–France Double Taxation Avoidance Convention (1958, amended)
Bilateral Investment Treaties negotiated through the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union covering over 100 jurisdictions
EU Single Market, Customs Union, and Common Commercial Policy framework

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the register of beneficial owners (UBO Register Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 17 January 2020 on the UBO register filing procedure; CSSF Circular 13/554 on professional AML/CFT obligations; Law of 5 August 2020 on the use of virtual IBAN and related due diligence protocols where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of deposit of the share capital for a Luxembourg SARL (Attestation de dépôt de capital)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg licensed credit institution holding the blocked incorporation account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank-issued attestation; if issued by a foreign bank under the contemplated documentary framework, it must be notarized, apostilled or consular-legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent home-country trade registry or corporate registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization at the Luxembourg diplomatic or consular post in the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney for the incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL granted to the notary and the representative of the shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or authorized corporate body of each corporate shareholder, or individual shareholder signature certified by a notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for corporate resolutions; individual signatures notarized then apostilled or consular-legalized if executed outside Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport photocopies, national identity cards, and proof of address of each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country passport authority or national migration registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copies in the home country followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the jurisdiction of issue

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories and known affiliated trading counterparties against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (CFUSF), UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists (including UNSCR 1267, 1718, 2231 and other relevant regimes), OFAC SDN list, United Kingdom sanctions list where relevant, the Luxembourg national asset-freeze list and international PEP databases; adverse media checks and enhanced due diligence must follow CSSF Circular 13/554 and Law of 12 November 2004; all screening must be documented and retained for a minimum of five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCSL interactive portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Latin script. Any non-Latin script corporate name or suggested commercial denomination must be transliterated into French, German, English, or Luxembourgish for registration. The official corporate name used in the articles of incorporation must correspond exactly to the name verified by the RCSL; the notary ensures orthographic consistency and prohibits any name causing confusion with an existing registered entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de commerce / Chamber of Commerce
Chambre des métiers / Chamber of Skilled Trades
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name refusal, the RCSL must issue a written decision stating the grounds. Applicants may first request an internal reconsideration through the LBR portal within 15 calendar days. If the refusal is maintained, or where the decision concerns a sensitive token requiring ministerial authorization, the applicant may lodge an administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification. The appeal must include the RCSL written refusal, the proposed name, and evidence of entitlement. If the rejection is based on an administrative omission, the applicant may also file a request for annulment or a declaratory action before the same tribunal according to the Code de procédure administrative.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and domiciliation arrangements are permitted on a provisional basis, but they cannot replace the statutory obligation to maintain a genuine registered office located in Luxembourg. For a specialty green coffee import SARL, the RCSL and tax authorities expect a physical address capable of receiving official notices, storing corporate records, and serving as the administrative seat. A pure virtual office without local administrative substance presents a significant compliance and substance risk; it should be replaced or supplemented by an executive office or licensed domiciliation provider ensuring physical presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; approximately 20% for a newly incorporated Luxembourg SARL in the wholesale coffee import/distribution sector during the first three years. Unannounced verification visits by the RCSL or the Administration des contributions directes may occur in connection with VAT registration, substance checks, or targeted AML/CFT controls.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL name pre-clearance, availability verification and sixty-day name blocking arranged through the Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary on behalf of Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial administrative charge and prevailing market rate for name availability services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notarial deed for incorporation of a société à responsabilité limitée, including drafting of articles, board minutes, share issue protocol and UBO statement annexes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and customary fee for a standard SARL incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL registration fee and publication of the notarial deed in the electronic company gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR administrative fee schedule for SARL filing, including RES publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing and mandatory beneficial ownership declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR electronic filing fee for UBO registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Blocked share-capital account attestation issued by a Luxembourg licensed credit institution for the minimum EUR 12,000 SARL capital requirement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service charge for blocked capital account opening and attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular or Hague apostille legalization bundle for foreign corporate and UBO documentation, assuming four documents requiring apostille/legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country apostille authorities and/or Luxembourg diplomatic or consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedules and prevailing apostille processing fees; four-document assumption

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of home-country constitutional, registry and identity documents into French for the notarial file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-sworn translator or licensed Luxembourg translation service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per page of certified translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT integrated PEP, sanctions, adverse-media, and UBO piercing due diligence report prepared by a Luxembourg qualified lawyer or compliance advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg legal counsel or AML/CFT compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional fee benchmark for pre-incorporation KYC and AML/CFT due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 1-14 and Articles 442-1 et seq. on the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (S.à r.l.); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register, as amended; Law of 16 May 2018 on the circulation of civil and commercial companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 14 rue Alphonse Weicker, L-2721 Luxembourg (online portal: lbr.lu)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authentic Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif authentique) including the Articles of Association (Statuts), filed electronically in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard S.à r.l. requires a statutory minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 (Law of 10 August 1915, Article 442-1(1), as amended), fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in kind at formation. The capital must be deposited in escrow in a blocked subscription account ('compte de souscription bloqué') opened with a CSSF-regulated credit institution in the name of the future company; the funds may be released only after RCS registration of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.À R.L. Adopted by the unanimous written consent of the managers on [DATE]. The Managers resolve: 1. Corporation: The deed of incorporation and Statuts accepted; EUR 12,000 share capital fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the banker's certificate. 2. Registered Office: The registered office is established at [ADDRESS], Luxembourg. 3. Officers: [NAME] is appointed Manager (Gérant); [NAME] appointed Assistant Manager. 4. Authorities: Each manager acting singly is authorized to complete all RCS registrations, RESA formalities, tax, social security and banking filings and to sign all documents. 5. Effective Date: This resolution is effective immediately and remains in force until amended. Certified by the Chairperson.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Structuring and Drafting of Notarial Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg) in coordination with Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary or corporate service provider; draft the Statuts (Articles), subscribe the EUR 12,000 share capital, fix the registered office address, identify the managers (gérants) and their acceptance; obtain name availability confirmation via the RCS name search and prepare the beneficial-ownership declaration template. The notary clears the draft against mandatory statutory clauses and professional formalities.
required_dossiers: Company name availability confirmation from RCS
Draft Articles of Association (Statuts)
Identity documents (passport/ID) of all shareholders, managers and ultimate beneficial owners
Indication of registered office address (projected lease or domiciliation agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS name search flags a conflict, propose and clear an alternative distinctive corporate name before signature. If the notary identifies non-compliant clauses, amend the draft Statuts by notarial correction and obtain shareholder re-approval prior to signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Escrow Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg-regulated credit institution supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the chosen bank to open a temporary blocked subscription account ('compte de souscription bloqué') in the name of the future S.à r.l.; each shareholder transfers its capital subscription in proportion to its quota; the bank issues a banker's certificate (attestation de libération des apports) confirming the deposit, addressed to the notary for the deed.
required_dossiers: Pre-drafted Statuts approved by the notary
Identification and KYC documentation for signatories and ultimate beneficial owners
Source-of-funds evidence for each capital subscription
Bank account instruction letter and IBAN confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML/source-of-wealth queries, provide audited account statements or independent wealth attestation. If the account cannot be opened, select an alternate CSSF-regulated bank and recommence the escrow instruction without material delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation and Statutory Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the constitution meeting before the Luxembourg notary; shareholders or their legal representatives sign the deed of incorporation; the notary verifies the banker's certificate, administers formal incorporation, and authenticates the Statuts. The company acquires separate legal personality only upon RCS registration, but execution preserves the applicable statutory signature deadline.
required_dossiers: Banker's certificate of capital liberation
Final deed draft and appendices approved by shareholders
Powers of attorney for any shareholder acting by representation
Signatory passports and current residence documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder cannot appear, the notary requires a duly notarized special power of attorney before signature. If the deed is rejected or suspended, execute a notarial rectification deed or re-notarize the instrument prior to RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Registration with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, 14 rue Alphonse Weicker, L-2721 Luxembourg (lbr.lu e-filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation dossier electronically within one month of the notarial deed date. The e-filing includes the authentic deed, written acceptance of office by each manager, registered office confirmation, and payment of the official RCS fee. Monitor dossier status via the LBR secure login until the RCS allocates the registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (authentic copy)
Written acceptance of appointment by each manager (Gérant)
Proof of availability and address of registered office
Receipt confirming payment of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or request for regularization, respond within the prescribed delay by uploading the corrected filing. If the one-month legal filing deadline is missed, instruct the notary to prepare a second notarial act rectifying the omission or extending the filing validity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Register (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Legilux - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the LBR automatically publishes the statutory excerpt and corporate particulars in the RESA on the Legilux platform. Verify the publication date because third-party effectiveness and the commencement of commercial operations run from the RESA publication. Apply for the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) if not automatically assigned.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate/extract containing the registration number
Electronic confirmation of RESA publication
LEI application form for legal entity identification, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact the LBR helpdesk and request priority processing. If the RESA excerpt contains errors, submit a corrective filing to the RCS and obtain a revised publication notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security and Establishment Permit Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AED); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des Classes Moyennes (SME Department)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of RCS registration, complete VAT and corporate income tax registration with the AED, including application for a Luxembourg VAT number; register with CCSS for social security if any employee is hired; and file the establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) application with the Ministry of Economy on the ground that the company conducts a commercial wholesale activity, submitting the manager's criminal record and professional qualification evidence.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate and RESA publication excerpt
AED VAT and corporate tax registration forms
Establishment permit application with CV and clean criminal record of the Gérant
Lease contract and floor plan of the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Economy queries the establishment permit file, supplement the missing exhibits (diploma equivalence, professional experience certificate, or amended lease). If VAT registration is delayed, the AED may grant a retroactive registration effect; file an extension request in writing to avoid late-filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commune, Food-Safety and Environmental Clearances for Warehousing Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Communal administration of the warehouse site; Administration luxembourgeoise de la sécurité alimentaire (ALVA); Administration de l'Environnement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify the commune of the low-impact class 4 classified establishment (établissement classé) used for dry storage of green coffee; obtain the required occupancy/operating permit if the premises are subject to urban-planning authorization; register as a food business operator with ALVA under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 for placing unroasted green coffee on the market; and prepare a simplified HACCP/pest-control plan for inspection readiness.
required_dossiers: Warehouse lease or ownership title
Floor plan and structural load certificate by an approved engineer
Fire-safety clearance from the communal fire commission or CGDIS
ALVA food business operator registration declaration (FBO-LU)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commune refuses the operating permit on zoning grounds, apply for a discretionary derogation or relocate the warehouse to a compatible logistics zone. If ALVA requests food-safety documentation, submit the HACCP manual, cleaning schedule, and pest-control records within 15 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des Classes Moyennes (Department for SMEs) acting for establishment permits; no sector-specific industrial licence applies to wholesale distribution of specialty green coffee beans under ISIC 4631.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'établissement) under the Luxembourg Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to crafts, commerce, and SMEs; no additional sectoral operating licence is required for the import and wholesale of green arabica coffee beans.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Administration - Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 4 notification regime (établissement classé) under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the licensing of classified establishments, as amended in 2018; full EIA report not required for warehousing and wholesale distribution of dried vegetable products such as green coffee beans.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant VOC or particulate emissions generated by green coffee handling; compliance required with communal wastewater by-laws for sanitary and cleaning water, Regulation (EC) 1935/2004 for food-contact storage materials, and the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; no hazardous-waste threshold applicable for dry bean storage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval from the communal fire-prevention commission or the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for the warehouse; structural load inspection certificate issued by a licensed engineer; workplace health-and-safety clearance under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 June 2003 by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM); and sanitary approval of the premises by ALVA in accordance with Regulation (EC) 852/2004.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: For direct taxation: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), managed via the Luxembourg government portal www.guichet.lu. For indirect taxation and VAT registration: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), also accessed through www.guichet.lu and the RCS (Luxembourg Business Registers) single digital gateway.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing or registering a Luxembourg SARL must first complete incorporation through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) and obtain a Luxembourg register number and LUID number. For VAT purposes, the entity must file a VAT registration application with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu or the prescribed paper form, providing statutory identification, registered office, activity codes (ISIC/NACE), anticipated turnover, and bank details. Upon review, the AEDT issues a Luxembourg national VAT identification number (numéro de TVA), typically within one month. Non-resident entities with no Luxembourg establishment but engaged in taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly with the AEDT or use the non-EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) / Union OSS where applicable. The same registration procedure is required before the entity can issue valid electronic invoices, claim input VAT, or conduct intra-community or export transactions with VAT identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' election. A SARL is hereby an opaque, entity-level taxable company subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICA), and net wealth tax (ISF). Available statutory elections include: (i) an option to form a VAT group per Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, which treats group members as a single taxable person; (ii) an election for tax consolidation (fiscal unity) under Article 164bis LIR for fully taxable resident companies; (iii) the option to apply the Luxembourg participation exemption regime for qualifying dividends and capital gains, subject to holding conditions; and (iv) elections regarding the application of ATAD hybrid mismatch rules, including the option to align treatment with a foreign branch or hybrid instrument where Luxembourg domestic law transposing EU Directive 2017/952 permits a balancing adjustment. No other pass-through election is available for a SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (excluding VAT) for the small enterprise exemption; registration is mandatory once taxable turnover exceeds this threshold, unless the entity voluntarily registers. Additional thresholds apply to distance sales of goods and intra-community acquisitions in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose a real-time fiscal clearance mandate, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping obligation for B2B invoicing. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing is required for supplies to Luxembourg central government entities, generally through the PEPPOL BIS network or a Luxembourg public sector e-invoicing platform. For all other invoices, structured electronic invoicing (e.g., EN16931/UBL) is acceptable but not mandatory. There is no requirement for pre-clearance via government API for B2B commercial transactions, including export sales of green coffee beans.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Luxembourg VAT-registered supplier may zero-rate (0% VAT) the supply of goods physically exported from the customs territory of the European Union to a destination outside the EU, including specialty green coffee beans, provided all applicable conditions are met: (i) the goods are dispatched or transported out of the European Union by the supplier or on behalf of the supplier; (ii) the departure is evidenced by an accepted customs export declaration (SAD) and, where applicable, proof of removal from the EU; and (iii) the supplier maintains full documentary substantiation in accordance with Article 243(1) of the Luxembourg VAT Law and the VAT Implementing Regulation (EU) No 282/2011. For services directly related to exported goods, or services supplied to non-EU customers, zero-rating or outside-scope rules may apply under standard place-of-supply provisions. The export zero-rating claim must be completed within the timeframe of 90 days from the time of supply, and the goods must be removed from the EU within that same period; otherwise VAT becomes chargeable at the standard rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / SAD) accepted and stamped by the customs office, or electronic export declaration through the Luxembourg ECS system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving transportation of the goods outside the European Union
Commercial invoice issued by the Luxembourg supplier
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or other bank payment evidence showing settlement of the export sale proceeds
Packing list and transport documents (CMR, sea waybill, air consignment note)
Proof of export within the required 90-day removal period, such as customs exit confirmation and, if applicable, documentary evidence from the destination country customs
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT authorities and the customs administration may perform stringent documentary and physical audits of export zero-rated supplies. If the exporter fails to produce valid export evidence, or where the export declaration is found to be fraudulent, the tax administration will reassess the VAT at the standard rate (17%) and issue a corrective invoice subject to late payment interest. Penalties include the cancellation of the zero-rated treatment, collection of the under-declared VAT, a fine of up to the amount of evaded tax, and in cases of intentional fraud, criminal prosecution before Luxembourg courts with potential imprisonment and additional administrative penalties. Retrospective clawbacks may apply to reopened assessments within the standard three-year limitation period, extended to ten years in cases of fraud or wilful attempt to evade tax. To preserve entitlement to zero-rating, the exporter must retain for at least ten years all supporting customs and transactional documentation evidencing physical removal of the goods from the EU.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and the European Central Bank (ECB) for Eurosystem matters
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: As a Eurozone member state, Luxembourg applies the EU free movement of capital regime; no exchange controls exist for current or capital account transactions; profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to standard corporate governance and tax compliance (withholding tax considerations on dividends), and no surrender or conversion requirements are imposed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender obligation; proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted freely; only standard anti-money laundering / anti-terrorist financing reporting thresholds apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility: EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) may passport into Luxembourg under the EU e-Money Directive and PSD2; however, due to the trade operations (documentary LCs, FX needs) and the requirement for a stable Luxembourg nexus, a traditional licensed credit institution is strongly preferred; EMIs cannot offer full trade finance products.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg authorities permit remote onboarding for legal entities under the AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) if the KYC standards are met; however, for non-resident directors or ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) from higher-risk jurisdictions, physical presence or a notarized power of attorney with certified identity documents may be required by local compliance teams; best practice assumes a physical board meeting for the initial banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) located in a high-risk third country (FATF call for increased attention)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, proof of source of wealth (3 years of bank statements, audited financial statements, tax returns), a group structure chart with full chain of ownership, and independent legal opinion confirming the economic substance of the SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex holding structure with multiple intermediary jurisdictions (e.g., offshore entities)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detail all entities in the ownership chain with jurisdiction-specific business rationale; obtain and present notarized board resolutions and signed declarations from each intermediary entity; provide the consolidated group annual report and transactional flow diagrams.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual or disproportionate transaction volumes relative to expected green coffee trade (commodity trading potential risk)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply-chain contracts, bills of lading, warehouse receipts, insurance certificates, and purchase/sale agreements; maintain a trade finance pack consistent with SWIFT MT103 or documentary LC flows; provide a budget and treasury forecast for the first 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between corporate purpose and intended banking transactions (e.g., rapid capital accumulation without clear commercial logic)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with EBITDA projections, market analysis, ISIC classification (4631) documentation, the Articles of Association, and board minutes approving the treasury mandate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder loans and equity contributions must be documented with a purpose code (e.g., BOP-Investment direct or Financial Credits); wire transfers to Luxembourg should use SWIFT MT103 with explicit remitter account and beneficiary account; for the SARL's capital account, reference the company registration number (RCS) and use the bank's internal purpose code 'Equity Subscription'; verification requires a notarized subscription deed and LuxTrust digital signature for residency validation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to coffee origin suppliers (e.g., Brazil, Ethiopia) are executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers or documentary Letters of Credit (LCs); for documentary LCs, the issuing Luxembourg bank arranges a sight or usance LC with documents: commercial invoice, certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate, bill of lading, and banking remittance advice; use ICC Uniform Customs and Practice (UCP600) standards.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Outright Forwards (deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/BRL, EUR/ETB)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or illiquid source-currency exposures
FX Swaps (swap of principal and interest in two currencies)
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for long-term financing hedging
FX Options (European-style calls/puts) with regulated Luxembourg or EU-licensed counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual financial statements (comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (Luxembourg Business Registers / LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within six months of the financial year-end; RCS filing within one month of approval. Calendar-year SARL: final filing no later than 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is a criminal offence for managers; fines up to EUR 25,000, judicial summons, coercive filing order, publication of non-compliance, and management liability; prolonged default after formal notices may lead to court-ordered strike-off or dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner (UBO) registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due no later than 31 December of each calendar year; any UBO change caused by share transfers or ownership restructures must be reported within one month of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual UBO confirmation triggers the mandatory publication of the company's name on the LBR non-compliance list, administrative fines, and criminal penalties up to EUR 25,000 under the Law of 13 January 2019; repeated omissions can lead to dissolution proceedings against the SARL and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax declaration (combined tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD – Luxembourg tax administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers: file by 31 May of the year following the business year; electronic filing through MyGuichet may be extended to 31 December. Non-calendar-year companies: file within five months after the accounting year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty for late filing ranges from EUR 750 to EUR 25,000, plus late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; ACD may issue an ex-officio assessment and enforce collection; serious tax offence risks criminal prosecution of the managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Internal statutory register audit and reconciliation of member/share transfer records with UBO declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company board of managers and registered domiciliation agent; no filing to a regulator, but constitutes supporting evidence for RCS and RBE filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per financial year before the general meeting approving the annual accounts, and immediately before filing any shareholder change to the RCS or RBE.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or inaccurate registers of members or share transfers are a criminal offence under Luxembourg commercial law; they impair evidentiary value in ownership disputes and expose managers to fines and civil liability. Defective registers may cause rejection of RCS/RBE filings and trigger UBO penalty proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit is required when the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 6.5 million, net turnover EUR 13 million, average headcount 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities, parent companies preparing consolidated accounts, and where shareholders representing 10% of the capital demand an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 and the Règlement grand-ducal of 5 December 2002 on annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used for consolidated accounts and is permitted for individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must keep its RBE declaration accurate at all times. Any transfer of shares or change in the percentage of voting rights or ownership must be declared to the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month. Independently of changes, the entity must perform a full annual confirmation before 31 December, verifying each beneficial owner's name, citizenship, residential address and ownership quote; the managers must sign the annual confirmation and record the review in the corporate minute book.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and ownership changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% central corporate income tax (IRC) plus 7% solidarity surcharge, aggregating to an 18.19% combined CIT headline; municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) adds approximately 6.75%–10.5% depending on commune
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first EUR 200,000 of taxable income (plus surcharge, effective 16.05%); participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; no broad tax holidays and no sector-specific incentives for coffee distribution

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1002 ('Corporate Income Tax, Municipal Business Tax and Net Wealth Tax Return') filed through the Luxembourg e-Tax platform via MyGuichet (guichet.lu)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, per tax year/corporate fiscal year-end
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 March of the year following the fiscal year for calendar-year companies (within 90 days of fiscal year-end for non-calendar-year companies); extensions are available on request, normally to 30 September, when the return is filed electronically by a registered tax adviser

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, RCS-Luxembourg registration number, full address, Luxembourg tax file number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use exact corporate register data; the Luxembourg appointed manager must sign, and no foreign tax identification number is required in this field

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss account items: turnover, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, depreciation, financial results
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the SARL's operating profit under Luxembourg GAAP; include global sourcing and shipping costs for containerized green-coffee deliveries, and attach an audited or certified P&L if total turnover exceeds EUR 2,500,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing declaration: disclose related-party transactions (goods, services, loans, intangible royalties) and method used
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check 'yes' if intercompany transactions exceed statutory thresholds (goods > EUR 5,000,000; services, interest, royalties, or loans > EUR 1,000,000) and attach Local File/Master File as applicable; describe the arm's-length CUP based on specialty green-coffee benchmark data

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax reconciliation for dividends and income subject to Luxembourg source withholding tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List gross dividends declared/repatriated to non-resident shareholders; claim 0% parent-subsidiary or DTA relief by attaching the shareholder's valid tax residence certificate and Form 90 declaration; if no relief applies, pay 15% withholding tax by the 10th day of the month following the distribution

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a coercive fine and a tax surcharge up to 25% of assessed tax; annual late-payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month on unpaid corporate income tax, capped at 10% per chargeable period; non-filing permits the tax administration to make an extraordinary default assessment and to prosecute directors in cases of unlawful refusal

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends paid by a Luxembourg SARL, unless exemption or treaty relief applies; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders holding a 10% participation for 12 unbroken months and under Luxembourg participation-exemption conditions
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must hold the shares for at least 12 months, submit a valid tax-residence certificate (TRC) to the Luxembourg paying agent or directly to the Administration des contributions directes (ACD), and file Form 90. The paying agent may apply the reduced rate at source only after prior administrative approval; excess withheld tax may be reclaimed within three years of the payment date
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no withholding tax on outbound arm's-length interest on standard trade/loan arrangements or on royalties paid to non-residents; treaty rates are generally 0% for interest and royalties. Exception: a 15% WHT applies to interest paid to Luxembourg-resident individuals or on dividend-like profit participation under certain hybrid instruments; standard coffee trade finance loans are not subject to Luxembourg WHT

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File/Master File must be maintained when the Luxembourg entity's related-party goods transactions exceed EUR 5,000,000, or other controlled transactions (services, interest, royalties, financial dealings) exceed EUR 1,000,000; Country-by-Country Report obligations arise when the consolidated group revenue is above EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' regime as found in UAE/offshore centres, but the ACD enforces substantive activity through OECD/ATAD anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership tests, and transfer-pricing substance assessments. A specialty green-coffee SARL must maintain local employees, premises, commercial decision-making, and risk management functions to benefit from treaty or parent-subsidiary relief; inadequate substance will cause treaty-benefit denial, reclassification of distributions, and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting coffee-container sales revenue, falsifying purchase invoices, mispricing intercompany margins, or disguising equity distributions as deductible interest to avoid Luxembourg corporate income tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to five years under the Luxembourg General Tax Law; civil assessment of the evaded tax, late interest, and an evasion penalty of 20%–100% of the tax evaded
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns and act contrary to the company's interests are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax; conviction results in civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / treaty abuse / artificial substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Luxembourg SARL predominantly to acquire tax residence and treaty or parent-subsidiary benefits without real office, personnel, local risk-taking, or economic functions; booking specialty-coffee margins in Luxembourg while all management is conducted outside the country
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under GAAR, denial of treaty benefits and parent-subsidiary relief, assessment of full domestic tax at 18.19% plus 15% dividend withholding tax on deemed distributions, and material-misstatement penalties of 5%–15%
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate a purely artificial Luxembourg entity face personal tax assessments, administrative restraining orders, restitution of taxes/interest/penalties, and repeated abuse may result in travel bans and extradition proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to disclose ultimate beneficial owners in Luxembourg's Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), use of nominee shareholders, or routing coffee-export sales proceeds through opaque shell jurisdictions to conceal profit repatriation activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 1,250,000 under Luxembourg AML laws (Law of 12 November 2004), sequestration and freezing of funds, imprisonment up to five years for money laundering, and delisting from the register of beneficial owners
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are subject to criminal prosecution, personal monetary fines measured by the laundered amount, travel bans, restrictions on bank account signatory authority, and disqualification as directors of Luxembourg financial institutions
